summary: Misaligned flush timing in continuous batcher causing sudden p99 latency waves
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Arcadia Health) reports intermittent but repeatable p95/p99 spikes for short streaming requests from a dedicated pool. Spikes present as sudden waves lasting ~30-90s where p95 jumps ~200-600ms and p99 spikes to multiple seconds (observed up to 6.1s). Impact: user-facing timeouts and a small increase in 504 errors during waves.

Impact:
- Multiple mid-sized customers experienced degraded experience for short chat turns (1-3 tokens per chunk) during windows.
- Billing and SLAs affected for dedicated pool customers during events.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (dgx-4 node type) in prod-us-east serving gptx-13b-quant-v2.
- Continuous/coalescing batcher enabled with tenant-priority weighting and adaptive linger.
- Observed primarily on nodes with mixed short-stream and long-stream traffic.

Observed behavior:
- Regular traffic baseline latency p95 ~120ms. During event windows p95 climbs to 400-800ms, p99 to 2-6s.
- Traces show many short streaming requests being held for additional linger periods and then flushed together, producing a burst of long flush time.
- Metrics show batch sizes increasing suddenly (from ~4->40) aligned with flush events.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous batcher should maintain smooth flush cadence for short streams without accumulating large micro-batches that cause long-tail spikes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route mixed traffic (short streaming turns interleaved with longer streams) through a dedicated pool with continuous batcher enabled.
2) Use a steady low-QPS short-stream workload (50-200 r/s) with occasional long streams present.
3) Observe p95/p99 over a 30-90 minute window and correlate batcher flush metrics (batch_size, flush_interval, queue_depth).
4) Compare behavior with/without tenant-priority weighting and with different min_flush_period settings.

comments: Support (Ayesha): Customer reported first seen 2026-03-09 evening. Attachting initial traces and Grafana snapshots. Asked for exact traffic pattern and whether any pool config changed.
Customer (Arcadia Health): Confirmed no config changes on their side. Pattern seems to happen more during QPS drops followed by small bursts.
SRE (Liam): Noticed batch_size surges and aligned flush timestamps across several hosts. Scheduling an investigation into host timer behavior and scheduler alignment logic.
Eng (Nia, runtime team): Suggested testing with monotonic clock usage and disable tenant-priority weighting to reproduce. Also asked for kernel and NTP status on affected nodes.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Flush timing alignment across hosts causes simultaneous coalescing of many short requests -> large micro-batches -> p99 waves.
Hypothesis 2: Host-level timer jitter (observed on node-03 and node-07) due to kernel frequency scaling (intel_pstate) caused drift in the software timer used by the coalescer.
Action: Pulled Grafana dashboards for batch_size, flush_interval, and per-host timer drift. Found correlation between hosts with higher timer jitter and stronger p99 spikes.

Experiment: Switched the batcher to use CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW in a canary pool and disabled tenant-priority weighting for 2h. Result: p99 tail reduced by ~45% during similar traffic windows and alignment events were fewer.

Logs/links: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/continuous-batcher?orgId=1&from=now-2h
Kernel logs: node-03: dmesg shows frequent CPU frequency transitions at time of events.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: rolled out a change to use a monotonic raw clock for the batcher timer and added randomized jitter to the flush alignment window to avoid cross-host synchronization.

Hotfix deployed to prod-us-east dedicated pool (rolling update across nodes) on 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC. Observed immediate reduction in event amplitude; p99 decreased from ~3.2s to ~1.4s in subsequent windows.
Permanent fix PR: github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-scheduler/pull/1109 — uses monotonic clock and introduces smoothing to adaptive linger calculation.
Workarounds for customers: temporary disable tenant-priority weighting or increase min_flush_period to smooth batching. Provided CLI examples to Arcadia Health.

Follow-ups: (1) Add per-host timer-jitter telemetry and alerting, (2) Update Continuous Batcher runbook with steps to diagnose alignment events, (3) Schedule kernel tuning audit for dedicated host images to reduce frequency scaling jitter.
